fields.acceptance: A testscript in a git repo commits with Change: <id> and Actor: builder, then writes Evidence verifying the change set's leaf: as builder, check --json exits 0 with one warn finding on rule evidence-actor naming the four; as verifier, no such finding; a commit with no Actor: trailer yields none. Go tests run the rule on given commit trailers, so check itself still runs no git.
fields.statement: rhiza check warns, on a rule named evidence-actor, for each live Evidence that verifies a capability when the Evidence's actor is named in an Actor: trailer of a commit that changes a file outside .rhiza/ and carries the Change: trailer of the change set that added that capability, unless the commit's Leaf: trailers name other leaves only. The warning names the Evidence, the capability, the actor and the commit. Outside a git work tree the rule is skipped, silently.
The evidence-actor rule counts only commits that change a file outside .rhiza/: a commit of model writes alone, such as ship's land commit or a verifier's Evidence commit, is not a leaf's code.
fields.wording: the agent's option, accepted by the owner when the final review found that .rhiza-only commits made every leaf warn after landing
